pathway.title: DAVITA INC. — Full credit assessment
pathway.question: Should we own this issuer, in which instrument, and why?

runs.text: The business is strong in scale and regulated revenue but narrow in profit. DaVita serves about 36% of U.S. dialysis patients, Medicare and Medicare Advantage pay 57% of U.S. dialysis patient service revenue, and no commercial payor exceeds 10% of revenue, but non-hospital commercial payors are 26% of revenue and 11% of patients and generate nearly all profits. Revenue is therefore durable in total and fragile in the part that earns the profit. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_dva-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 11; 10-K_2025-12-31_dva-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 15; 10-K_2025-12-31_dva-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 117; 10-K_2025-12-31_dva-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 172; Business & governance (CP-1A)

Cash generation is adequate but thinner than EBITDA suggests. Free cash flow before partner distributions was 47.50% of EBITDA in FY2025 and 45.90% in the last twelve months, and the issuer’s own measure was 37.12% in FY2025. Cash interest and cash taxes took 25.09% of EBITDA in FY2025, and cash taxes were unusually low, so a normal year converts less. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2025-12-31_dva-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 114; 10-K_2025-12-31_dva-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 128; 10-K_2025-12-31_dva-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 213; calculation B01; calculation B02

Margins are being squeezed. EBITDA margin fell from 21.96% in FY2024 to 19.90% in the last twelve months, because patient care cost per treatment rose faster than revenue per treatment while treatments were flat. Medicare rate updates of 2.2% for 2026 and an estimated 2.7% for 2027 do not close that gap. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_dva-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 13; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dva-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 37; calculation B03

Leverage has drifted up and has little room before the 4.00x line. Debt to EBITDA rose from 3.36x at FY2024 to 3.72x at FY2025 and 3.82x at 2026-09-30. The issuer’s own ratio is 3.38x against a 3.0x to 3.5x target; a 15.61% fall in Consolidated EBITDA at unchanged debt would take that ratio to 4.00x, which is arithmetic on printed figures, not a covenant test. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2025-12-31_dva-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 114; 10-K_2025-12-31_dva-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 183; EX-99.1_2026-10-29_dva93026ex991.htm.jsonl, page 13; EX-99.1_2026-10-29_dva93026ex991.htm.jsonl, page 15; calculation B04; calculation B05

Liquidity is adequate near term and the 2030 and 2031 maturities are the real refinancing test. Cash and undrawn revolver cover debt due before 2028 13.27x, but the 2030 and 2031 maturities are 2.96x last-twelve-months EBITDA and 76.95% of principal, and the secured term loan and revolver fall due on 2030-03-02 if the 2030 senior notes remain outstanding. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_dva-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 11; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dva-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 12; calculation B06; calculation B07

Financial policy is the main governance risk. Repurchases were 1.75x issuer free cash flow in 2025 and 1.28x in nine months 2026, and repurchases plus partner distributions were 1.24x free cash flow before distributions in nine months 2026. No dividend, sponsor fee or creditor-adverse transaction is documented, and the 2026 buyback pace is lower. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation B08

Interest cost is protected to 2028 but not through the wall. Interest rate caps cover floating-rate debt with notional of USD 3,500 million through 2028, USD 3,000 million in 2029 and USD 500 million in 2030, so about USD 38.94 million per 100 bp is exposed on balances unchanged after 2029. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_dva-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 12; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dva-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 13; calculation B09

runs.text: Strengths are ranked first. The strongest support is scale and a regulated, recurring revenue base: DaVita serves about 36% of U.S. dialysis patients and Medicare and Medicare Advantage pay 57% of U.S. dialysis patient service revenue, so cash flow is visible and no single commercial payor exceeds 10% of revenue, which supports debt service through a downturn in commercial mix. The second is cash generation with low capital intensity: free cash flow before partner distributions was 47.50% of EBITDA in FY2025 and maintenance capital expenditure was USD 412 million, which leaves cash for debt service or buybacks. The third is liquidity and a light maturity ladder to 2029: cash and undrawn revolver cover debt due before 2028 13.27x. The fourth is interest cost protection to 2028 through caps with notional of USD 3,500 million, and the fifth is transparent reporting with no documented sponsor extraction. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_dva-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 11; 10-K_2025-12-31_dva-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 15; 10-K_2025-12-31_dva-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 117; 10-K_2025-12-31_dva-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 135; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dva-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 12; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dva-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 13; EX-99.1_2026-10-29_dva93026ex991.htm.jsonl, page 15; calculation B01; calculation B07

Weaknesses are ranked first. The largest is profit concentration in commercial payors, which are 26% of revenue and 11% of patients but generate nearly all profits, while the commercial mix is under pressure from expired tax credits. The second is leverage drift with buybacks above free cash flow: debt to EBITDA of 3.82x and a negative total equity, with the issuer ratio 0.62x below the 4.00x line. The third is the 2030 and 2031 maturity concentration, 2.96x last-twelve-months EBITDA, with a springing date of 2030-03-02. The fourth is margin pressure: EBITDA margin fell to 19.90% against flat volumes. The fifth is partner distributions and puts that rank ahead of creditors, with open legal matters unquantified. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_dva-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 15; 10-K_2025-12-31_dva-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 183; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dva-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 12; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dva-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 32; calculation B03; calculation B06

blocks.title: Transaction summary and new debt issues

runs.text: The company completed three financing steps in 2025 and one in 2026. It issued USD 1,000 million of 6.75% senior notes due 2033 on 2025-05-23, refinanced Term Loan B-1 and Term Loan A-1 through the Seventh and Eighth Amendments in July and November 2025 into Term Loan B-2 and Term Loan A-2 of USD 2,000 million with a new revolving credit facility of up to USD 1,500 million, and on 2026-06-08 added USD 500 million to Term Loan B-2 to repay part of the revolver. The refinancings pushed maturities to 2030 and 2031, where the debt wall now sits. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_dva-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 129; 10-K_2025-12-31_dva-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 181; 10-K_2025-12-31_dva-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 182; 10-K_2025-12-31_dva-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 184; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dva-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 12

The Berkshire Hathaway repurchase agreement of 2024-04-30 is the main equity transaction. It required settlements of USD 199.940 million on 2026-01-29, USD 182.865 million on 2026-05-01, USD 36.513 million on 2026-07-31 and USD 69.026 million on 2026-10-27, the last after the balance sheet date. Total repurchases from 2026-10-01 to 2026-10-27 were USD 86.703 million, and USD 1,212.423 million of authorisation remained on 2026-10-27. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_dva-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 200; 10-K_2025-12-31_dva-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 201; 10-Q_2026-03-31_dva-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 18; 10-Q_2026-06-30_dva-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 17; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dva-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 19

Acquisitions were modest: Fresenius Medical Care’s Brazil dialysis operations for initial consideration of USD 94.282 million effective 2025-08-01, and a USD 200 million Elara Caring minority interest that closed on 2026-07-20. No new debt issue or transaction after 2026-10-29 is supplied. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_dva-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 203; 10-Q_2026-06-30_dva-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 22; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dva-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 10

fields.value: Financial foundation for DAVITA INC. as of 2026-11-05 on the credit snapshot pathway. fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The issuer measures leverage differently, and its measure is the one the credit agreement uses. Its ratio of 3.38x uses principal, cash including short-term investments and Consolidated EBITDA of 3042 USD millions, so it sits 0.26x below the house net figure of 3.64x and 0.44x below the house total-debt figure of 3.82x, and it stays inside the 3.0x to 3.5x range the issuer calls its target. The annual report says the credit agreement lifts many limits on investments, share repurchases, dividends and further debt while the ratio is below 4.00x and sets the maximum at 5.00x through 2028 and 4.50x afterwards; the third-quarter release still prints 5.00x as the maximum, but neither quarterly report restates the 4.00x test or the step-down after the June 2026 amendment. The 0.62x between the issuer’s ratio and 4.00x is therefore a reading of a printed ratio against earlier text, not a verified covenant calculation, and no headroom is read from the house figures.

fields.value: Coverage is thinner than at the end of 2024. Cash interest cover fell from 6.65x in FY2024 to 5.35x in FY2025 because EBITDA slipped by 1.97% while cash interest paid rose from 423.360 to 515.497 US$m. Interim cash interest is not printed, so interim cover is not established; on accrued debt expense the cover is 4.76x for FY2025 and 4.75x for the last twelve months. The strongest offset is cash generation: operating cash flow of 1870.456 US$m over the last twelve months leaves 1293.703 US$m after capital expenditure, but the issuer deducts distributions to noncontrolling interests and prints free cash flow of 980 USD millions for the same period, which is the figure available to DaVita Inc.

fields.value: Liquidity is adequate near term but lower than at year end. At 2026-09-30 cash of 495.629 US$m and the undrawn revolver of 1420 US$m total 1915.629 US$m, against 144.409 US$m of debt due in the rest of 2026 and 2027; the same measure was 2176.438 US$m at 2025-12-31 because cash fell by 180.809 US$m as repurchases outran free cash flow. A separate bilateral facility carries 184.758 US$m of letters of credit and is not netted. The company states that 1212.423 US$m of repurchase authorisation remained at 2026-10-27 and that it remains subject to share repurchase limitations under its credit facilities, so the pace of repurchases is a management choice that bears directly on this cushion.

fields.value: The maturity profile is back-loaded. Only 451.705 US$m falls due from late 2026 to 2029, then 4570.280 US$m in 2030 and 3765.117 US$m in 2031, together 76.95% of principal. Term Loan A-2 and the revolver mature on 2030-11-24 but fall due on 2030-03-02 if any of the 4.625% senior notes remain outstanding 91 days before their 2030-06-01 maturity, so the 2030 refinancing must be completed ahead of the stated dates. Floating-rate balances of 4394.456 US$m are mostly capped: interest rate caps cover 3500 USD millions of notional through 2028, 3000 USD millions in 2029 and 500 USD millions in 2030, which leaves 894.456 US$m (Term Loan A-2 above the capped amount, and the drawn revolver) open to SOFR now and leaves little hedge in place when the 2030 and 2031 maturities arrive.

fields.value: Claims outside debt matter for creditors. The Berkshire repurchase obligation was a payable of 54.714 US$m at 2026-09-30; it grew with further open-market repurchases and was settled for 69.026 US$m on 2026-10-27. Total equity is a deficit of 358.466 US$m, and the deficit attributable to DaVita Inc. shareholders is 591.087 US$m, so there is no accounting cushion beneath the debt.

fields.value: A supported downside sequence starts in price and unit cost: revenue per treatment fell from 422.60 USD in the fourth quarter of 2025 to 415.25 USD in the third quarter of 2026, while patient care cost per treatment moved from 279.60 to 280.22 USD. Lower EBITDA would raise leverage first, then cut cover, while buybacks and distributions continue to compete for cash. fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Medium: EBITDA is not stated by the issuer in unadjusted form, so EBITDA (Reported) is house-calculated as operating income plus depreciation and amortization, and the issuer’s Consolidated EBITDA is printed only for the last twelve months at 2025-12-31 and later quarter ends. The adjusted period cells in the income statement, the adjusted ratios for 2024-12-31 and the bridge from the house measure to Consolidated EBITDA are not supplied, and the issuer’s printed add-backs sum to 3043 against 3042 USD millions. Leverage on the issuer’s measure is therefore shown at four dates only; the EBITDA bridge chart carries no figures until the unrounded add-backs are available.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Medium: Cash interest paid is printed only in the annual report, so interest cover on cash interest is stated for FY2024 and FY2025 and is not established for interim periods or the last twelve months. An accrual-based cover on debt expense is shown beside it. Interim cover would need cash interest paid for the nine months of 2026 and 2025.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Medium: The issuer prints net debt two ways in every release, and house net debt at 2026-09-30 differs from both: 10337 USD millions on principal net of cash and cash equivalents, and 10269 USD millions as Consolidated net debt with cash including short-term investments, against 10273.486 US$m on carrying value. The size of the deferred compensation exclusion in the issuer’s cash is not stated. All figures are kept; the house figure drives the charts and no covenant definition is chosen.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Medium: The executed credit agreement and indentures are not in the source set, so instrument-level carrying values, the scheduled amortisation of Term Loan B-2 and of the senior notes, call terms, baskets and covenant definitions are not established; each instrument keeps its disclosed principal and an aggregate financing cost adjustment of 63.128 US$m reconciles to carrying value. Facility-level security and ranking come from the filing descriptions only, and the 4.00x restriction test and the 4.50x step-down come from the annual report and are not restated after the June 2026 amendment. This restricts any conclusion on amortisation cash needs, refinancing cost or covenant capacity. The source readiness module rates the missing documents MATERIAL for covenant and priority work; for the financial statements here they limit only instrument detail, so the gap is rated Medium for this module.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Business and governance review of DAVITA INC. as of 2026-11-05 on the credit snapshot pathway. Scope: business and operating model, ownership and control, transactions and capital allocation, and governance and sponsor behaviour, from the seven supplied filings and releases and the supplied source readiness analysis.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Creditors rely on a Medicare-anchored dialysis franchise whose profit rests mainly on commercial payors, and governance risk is Medium because buybacks exceed free cash flow and partner distributions come first, not because any sponsor extracts value.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Non-hospital commercial payors are 26% of U.S. dialysis patient service revenue and 11% of patients yet generate nearly all profits. Repurchases of USD 1,788 million in 2025 against free cash flow of USD 1,024 million came while principal debt rose by USD 833 million, although the 2026 pace is 40.57% lower. Berkshire Hathaway received 27.10% of those repurchase dollars under a contract that holds it at 45.0%, and its actual holding is not stated.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_dva-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 15; 10-K_2025-12-31_dva-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 114; 10-K_2025-12-31_dva-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 179; 10-K_2025-12-31_dva-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 199; 10-K_2025-12-31_dva-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 200; calculation A04; calculation A05; calculation A06

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Profit is more concentrated than revenue. Non-hospital commercial payors are about 26% of U.S. dialysis patient service revenue and 11% of patients, yet the company says they generate nearly all profits, while Medicare and Medicare Advantage supply 57% of revenue and Medicare rates are set by regulation. The company reports that the end of enhanced premium tax credits hurt its commercial mix in 2026, so a small shift of patients out of commercial plans removes more profit than revenue. Profit by payor class is not disclosed, so the sensitivity cannot be sized.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Growth comes from price and acquisitions, and unit costs are catching up. Treatments fell 1.1% in 2025 and rose 0.5% in nine months 2026, while patient care cost per treatment rose 5.9% against revenue per treatment up 4.7% in 2025, lifting clinic cost from 65.96% to 66.74% of revenue per treatment. The nine-month 2026 share is 67.09% against 66.95%. Clinical wage rates rose about 3.8%, and Medicare rate updates of 2.2% for 2026 and an estimated 2.7% for 2027 sit below the 3.0% rise in cost per treatment in nine months 2026.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: International and ancillary growth adds scale at a lower margin and more variance. International revenue grew 37.8% to USD 1,346 million at a 6.61% operating margin against 17.67% for U.S. dialysis, and a goodwill and asset impairment of USD 62 million in China in Q3 2026 shows acquired value can be written down. Integrated kidney care takes medical cost risk through shared savings and shared losses arrangements.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_dva-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 7; 10-K_2025-12-31_dva-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 123; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dva-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 10; calculation A02; calculation A03

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Ownership is dispersed, but one holder shapes buyback cash. Berkshire Hathaway sells shares to the company each quarter so that it is held at 45.0%, and received 27.10% of 2025 repurchase dollars and 48.62% of nine-month 2026 repurchase dollars. Its standstill limits efforts to influence control, no dividend has been paid since 1994 and no sponsor fee appears in the sources, so no sponsor extraction is documented and no sponsor support can be assumed.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Shareholder returns have exceeded free cash flow and debt has risen, although the pace is slowing. Repurchases were 1.75x free cash flow in 2025 and 1.28x in nine months 2026, and principal debt rose USD 833 million in 2025 and USD 487.66 million in nine months 2026. Many credit agreement limits on repurchases fall away while the issuer-defined leverage ratio is below 4.00x, and that ratio is 3.38x, so management’s 3.0x to 3.5x target, not the credit agreement, is the more likely constraint on buybacks.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_dva-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 114; 10-K_2025-12-31_dva-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 179; 10-K_2025-12-31_dva-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 183; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dva-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 11; EX-99.1_2026-10-29_dva93026ex991.htm.jsonl, page 13; calculation A04; calculation A06

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Partner distributions are a second leak of cash. Payments to joint venture partners were 0.98x their income in 2025 and 1.21x in nine months 2026, and puts on partner interests are exercisable at the owners’ discretion, so a share of consolidated cash is committed to physician and hospital partners ahead of creditors.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_dva-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 194; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dva-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dva-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 3; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dva-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 4; calculation A08

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Reporting quality is good and legal exposure is open and unquantified. Audited statements carry an unqualified opinion, the audit, nominating and compensation committees are independent, and each release prints the credit agreement leverage ratio, but a qui tam false claims case, federal trade inquiries and state inquiries remain open, recorded accruals are immaterial and no range of loss is given.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest evidence against a Medium reading is that the company states a credit agreement leverage ratio of 3.38x inside its 3.0x to 3.5x target, has paid no dividend, discloses no sponsor fee or creditor-adverse transaction, cut repurchases by 40.57% in nine months 2026 and holds USD 1,420 million undrawn on its revolver. Medicare and Medicare Advantage also supply 57% of U.S. dialysis patient service revenue, and Medicare rate updates are 2.2% for 2026 and an estimated 2.7% for 2027.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The view would move toward Low if repurchases fell to or below free cash flow with principal debt flat and the proxy statement showed no related-party leakage. It would move toward High if repurchases kept exceeding free cash flow while the issuer ratio approached 4.00x, if commercial mix fell further, if the qui tam case or the federal trade inquiry produced a material penalty or a change in physician non-compete practice, or if Berkshire’s holding or standstill terms changed.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The 2026 proxy statement is not supplied, so board composition, executive pay, director and officer holdings and related-party dealings are not established; the Medium governance risk level cannot be moved to Low on documented governance alone.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Berkshire’s actual holding is not stated, so the size of the contractual cash call can be read only from amounts already settled; the finding that the agreement ties buyback cash to one holder rests on the 45.0% cap and the settlements, not on a projected stake.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Profit by payor class is not disclosed, so the statement that commercial payors generate nearly all profits is management’s and the sensitivity of earnings to a mix shift is described, not sized.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Funding sources for repurchases and acquisitions are not disclosed, so the conclusion that buybacks were debt-funded rests on repurchases exceeding free cash flow while principal debt rose, not on a stated source.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_dva-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 114; 10-K_2025-12-31_dva-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 179; calculation A04; calculation A06

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The 4.00x level below which many limits on repurchases fall away is taken from the annual report summary and is not restated in later quarterly reports after the June 2026 amendment, so the finding that repurchases are constrained mainly above that level may be incomplete.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Open legal and regulatory matters carry no loss estimate, so the governance risk level excludes any penalty and a material outcome could raise it.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The business is one large regulated dialysis line with smaller, lower-margin lines beside it, so U.S. dialysis profit sets the credit.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The company is a widely held public issuer with one large holder bound by contract, so no sponsor support can be assumed and no sponsor extraction is documented.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The company completed three financing steps in 2025 and one in 2026. It issued USD 1,000 million of 6.75% senior notes due 2033 on 2025-05-23, refinanced Term Loan B-1 and Term Loan A-1 through the Seventh and Eighth Amendments in July and November 2025 into Term Loan B-2 and Term Loan A-2 of USD 2,000 million with a new revolving credit facility of up to USD 1,500 million, and on 2026-06-08 added USD 500 million to Term Loan B-2 to repay part of the revolver. The refinancings pushed maturities to 2030 and 2031, where the debt wall now sits.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The Berkshire Hathaway repurchase agreement of 2024-04-30 is the main equity transaction. It required settlements of USD 199.940 million on 2026-01-29, USD 182.865 million on 2026-05-01, USD 36.513 million on 2026-07-31 and USD 69.026 million on 2026-10-27, the last after the balance sheet date. Total repurchases from 2026-10-01 to 2026-10-27 were USD 86.703 million, and USD 1,212.423 million of authorisation remained on 2026-10-27.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Acquisitions were modest: Fresenius Medical Care’s Brazil dialysis operations for initial consideration of USD 94.282 million effective 2025-08-01, and a USD 200 million Elara Caring minority interest that closed on 2026-07-20. No new debt issue or transaction after 2026-10-29 is supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Sponsor / Governance Risk Level: Medium. The level is driven by repurchases that exceed free cash flow and by partner distributions that rank ahead of creditors, because they leave debt high relative to earnings, which implies thinner refinancing capacity for the 2030 and 2031 maturities. Countervailing evidence is the absence of dividends, sponsor fees or creditor-adverse transactions, a leverage ratio inside the company’s target range and slower buybacks in 2026.

fields.value: Every operand is a printed figure in USD millions unless the row says otherwise; ratios are rounded to two decimals.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: DaVita’s fundamental credit is adequate but thinning: steady Medicare-anchored cash flow supports debt of 3.82x last-twelve-months EBITDA, yet buybacks run ahead of free cash flow and 76.95% of principal falls due in 2030 and 2031.

fields.value: Net of cash, leverage is 3.64x, or 3.68x pro forma for repurchases through 2026-10-27. Profit rests on a small commercial patient group, volumes are flat and unit costs are rising, so the primary downside is a commercial-mix and cost squeeze that pushes leverage toward the 4.00x level where covenant limits on buybacks return.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_dva-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 15; 10-K_2025-12-31_dva-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 183

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The business is strong in scale and regulated revenue but narrow in profit. DaVita serves about 36% of U.S. dialysis patients, Medicare and Medicare Advantage pay 57% of U.S. dialysis patient service revenue, and no commercial payor exceeds 10% of revenue, but non-hospital commercial payors are 26% of revenue and 11% of patients and generate nearly all profits. Revenue is therefore durable in total and fragile in the part that earns the profit.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_dva-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 11; 10-K_2025-12-31_dva-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 15; 10-K_2025-12-31_dva-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 117; 10-K_2025-12-31_dva-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 172; Business & governance (CP-1A)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Cash generation is adequate but thinner than EBITDA suggests. Free cash flow before partner distributions was 47.50% of EBITDA in FY2025 and 45.90% in the last twelve months, and the issuer’s own measure was 37.12% in FY2025. Cash interest and cash taxes took 25.09% of EBITDA in FY2025, and cash taxes were unusually low, so a normal year converts less.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2025-12-31_dva-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 114; 10-K_2025-12-31_dva-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 128; 10-K_2025-12-31_dva-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 213; calculation B01; calculation B02

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Margins are being squeezed. EBITDA margin fell from 21.96% in FY2024 to 19.90% in the last twelve months, because patient care cost per treatment rose faster than revenue per treatment while treatments were flat. Medicare rate updates of 2.2% for 2026 and an estimated 2.7% for 2027 do not close that gap.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_dva-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 13; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dva-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 37; calculation B03

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Leverage has drifted up and has little room before the 4.00x line. Debt to EBITDA rose from 3.36x at FY2024 to 3.72x at FY2025 and 3.82x at 2026-09-30. The issuer’s own ratio is 3.38x against a 3.0x to 3.5x target; a 15.61% fall in Consolidated EBITDA at unchanged debt would take that ratio to 4.00x, which is arithmetic on printed figures, not a covenant test.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2025-12-31_dva-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 114; 10-K_2025-12-31_dva-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 183; EX-99.1_2026-10-29_dva93026ex991.htm.jsonl, page 13; EX-99.1_2026-10-29_dva93026ex991.htm.jsonl, page 15; calculation B04; calculation B05

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Liquidity is adequate near term and the 2030 and 2031 maturities are the real refinancing test. Cash and undrawn revolver cover debt due before 2028 13.27x, but the 2030 and 2031 maturities are 2.96x last-twelve-months EBITDA and 76.95% of principal, and the secured term loan and revolver fall due on 2030-03-02 if the 2030 senior notes remain outstanding.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_dva-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 11; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dva-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 12; calculation B06; calculation B07

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Financial policy is the main governance risk. Repurchases were 1.75x issuer free cash flow in 2025 and 1.28x in nine months 2026, and repurchases plus partner distributions were 1.24x free cash flow before distributions in nine months 2026. No dividend, sponsor fee or creditor-adverse transaction is documented, and the 2026 buyback pace is lower.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation B08

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Interest cost is protected to 2028 but not through the wall. Interest rate caps cover floating-rate debt with notional of USD 3,500 million through 2028, USD 3,000 million in 2029 and USD 500 million in 2030, so about USD 38.94 million per 100 bp is exposed on balances unchanged after 2029.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest evidence against an adequate-but-thinning view is that the issuer’s own ratio of 3.38x sits inside its 3.0x to 3.5x target, buybacks fell 40.57% in nine months 2026, last-twelve-months EBITDA is 2.17% above FY2025, liquidity covers near-term maturities 13.27x, and Medicare and Medicare Advantage supply 57% of revenue at rates updated by regulators.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_dva-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 11; 10-K_2025-12-31_dva-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 114; EX-99.1_2026-10-29_dva93026ex991.htm.jsonl, page 13

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The view would strengthen if buybacks stayed at or below free cash flow with debt flat, if commercial mix held at about 11% of patients, and if the 2030 senior notes were refinanced early. It would weaken if EBITDA margin kept falling below 19.90%, if the issuer ratio approached 4.00x, if revolver draws rose, if the qui tam case or the federal trade inquiry brought a material penalty, or if the 2030 and 2031 maturities had to be refinanced after a mix or rate shock.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2025-12-31_dva-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 15; 10-K_2025-12-31_dva-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 183; 10-K_2025-12-31_dva-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 191; 10-K_2025-12-31_dva-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 192; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dva-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 12

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - No agency rating, market price or spread is supplied, so refinancing capacity rests on maturity structure and liquidity alone and cannot be tested against market access; the conclusion that the 2030 and 2031 wall is the main test could be softened or hardened by market conditions.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Covenant definitions, compliance certificates and the executed credit agreement are not supplied, so the distance to 4.00x and 5.00x is arithmetic on the issuer’s printed figures and the 4.00x test is read from the annual report; actual headroom may differ.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Profit by payor class is not disclosed, so the downside from commercial-mix loss is described as a causal path and is not sized in earnings.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - There is no forward model: the outlook rests on management’s 2026 guidance, announced Medicare rates and the issuer’s volume expectation, so the thinning view is a trend reading, not a projection.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Cash interest paid is printed only for fiscal years and FY2025 cash taxes were unusually low, so free cash flow conversion of 45.90% may overstate a normal year and interim interest cover is not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The annual report says the company may borrow to finance repurchases, but the funding of actual repurchases is not stated, so the link between buybacks and rising debt is inferred from cash flows.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Strengths are ranked first. The strongest support is scale and a regulated, recurring revenue base: DaVita serves about 36% of U.S. dialysis patients and Medicare and Medicare Advantage pay 57% of U.S. dialysis patient service revenue, so cash flow is visible and no single commercial payor exceeds 10% of revenue, which supports debt service through a downturn in commercial mix. The second is cash generation with low capital intensity: free cash flow before partner distributions was 47.50% of EBITDA in FY2025 and maintenance capital expenditure was USD 412 million, which leaves cash for debt service or buybacks. The third is liquidity and a light maturity ladder to 2029: cash and undrawn revolver cover debt due before 2028 13.27x. The fourth is interest cost protection to 2028 through caps with notional of USD 3,500 million, and the fifth is transparent reporting with no documented sponsor extraction.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_dva-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 11; 10-K_2025-12-31_dva-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 15; 10-K_2025-12-31_dva-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 117; 10-K_2025-12-31_dva-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 135; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dva-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 12; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dva-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 13; EX-99.1_2026-10-29_dva93026ex991.htm.jsonl, page 15; calculation B01; calculation B07

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Weaknesses are ranked first. The largest is profit concentration in commercial payors, which are 26% of revenue and 11% of patients but generate nearly all profits, while the commercial mix is under pressure from expired tax credits. The second is leverage drift with buybacks above free cash flow: debt to EBITDA of 3.82x and a negative total equity, with the issuer ratio 0.62x below the 4.00x line. The third is the 2030 and 2031 maturity concentration, 2.96x last-twelve-months EBITDA, with a springing date of 2030-03-02. The fourth is margin pressure: EBITDA margin fell to 19.90% against flat volumes. The fifth is partner distributions and puts that rank ahead of creditors, with open legal matters unquantified.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_dva-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 15; 10-K_2025-12-31_dva-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 183; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dva-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 12; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dva-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 32; calculation B03; calculation B06

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: DaVita is the largest U.S. dialysis provider by patients served, with about 36% of the market, and earns about 86% of revenue from U.S. dialysis through 2,657 outpatient centers at the end of 2025. The rest is integrated kidney care, other ancillary services and international dialysis, which together are about 14% of revenue and grew 27.3% in 2025, mainly abroad. Patients typically need three treatments a week for as long as they live or until a transplant, Medicare has covered dialysis since 1972 under a single bundled rate, and 89% of U.S. patients are on a government program, so volume and cash flow are visible even though price is not set by DaVita.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_dva-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 5; 10-K_2025-12-31_dva-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-K_2025-12-31_dva-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 12; 10-K_2025-12-31_dva-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 116; 10-K_2025-12-31_dva-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 117

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: That visibility supports debt service, but profit is less diversified than revenue: the company says commercial payors generate nearly all profits and that Medicare rates are, on average, significantly lower, so cash-flow durability rests on keeping commercial patients rather than on the number of patients served. Refinancing confidence therefore depends on commercial mix as much as on scale.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: DaVita is a widely held public company with no controlling sponsor. Berkshire Hathaway holds a stake that the filings do not size; a repurchase agreement requires DaVita to buy shares from Berkshire to hold it at 45.0% and a standstill limits its influence over control. Borrowers and guarantors are DaVita Inc. and its domestic subsidiaries, with the secured facilities ranking senior to the senior notes, and joint venture partners hold minority stakes in centers that supply about 30% of U.S. dialysis revenue.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_dva-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 16; 10-K_2025-12-31_dva-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 183; 10-K_2025-12-31_dva-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 200; 10-K_2025-12-31_dva-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 202

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The financial-policy consequence is that creditors face a company-managed shareholder-return policy, not a sponsor: leverage tolerance is stated as a 3.0x to 3.5x target on the issuer’s own definition, buybacks have exceeded free cash flow, and no dividend, sponsor fee or creditor-adverse transaction is documented. The governance risk level is Medium on that evidence.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Revenue is predictable, regulated and flat in volume. Treatments fell 1.1% in 2025 and rose 0.5% in nine months 2026 while revenue per treatment rose 4.7% in 2025 and 2.7% in nine months 2026, with the Medicare base rate rising 2.2% for 2026 and an estimated 2.7% for 2027. Price is therefore the growth driver and is set by regulators for 57% of revenue and negotiated with commercial payors for the profit-bearing part.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The risk mechanism is a mix shift, not a volume collapse: payors have tried plan designs that limit commercial coverage after the Supreme Court’s Marietta decision, enhanced premium tax credits expired at the end of 2025 and reduced exchange enrollment and commercial mix, and each commercial patient who moves to Medicare is paid a lower rate. Substitution by transplantation, home therapy or drugs such as GLP-1 receptor agonists is a slower risk to volume. The implication is that revenue is durable in total and exposed in its most profitable part.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Margins are being squeezed. Clinical labor, supplies and fixed center costs make up patient care cost, which rose 5.9% per treatment in 2025 against revenue per treatment up 4.7%, lifting clinic cost from 65.96% to 66.74% of revenue per treatment, and the nine-month 2026 share is 67.09%. EBITDA margin fell from 21.96% to 19.90% on the house measure, and international operations earn a 6.61% operating margin against 17.67% for U.S. dialysis.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation B03

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Margins can be defended only partly under volume pressure or wage inflation: the company reports clinical wage rates up about 3.8% in each of 2025 and 2024, productivity gains from lower turnover and cost initiatives, and a union organizing push in California, while Medicare rate updates are below cost growth. The implication is a slow decline in EBITDA margin unless commercial mix and productivity offset cost inflation.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Capital intensity is low and cash conversion is adequate. Capital spending was USD 575.864 million in FY2025, of which maintenance was USD 412 million, and operating cash flow was USD 1,886.5 million. Free cash flow before partner distributions was 47.50% of EBITDA, and the issuer’s own measure, after distributions, was 37.12%; cash interest and cash taxes together took 25.09% of EBITDA, with cash taxes 54.45% lower than in FY2024.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2025-12-31_dva-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 114; 10-K_2025-12-31_dva-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 128; 10-K_2025-12-31_dva-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 135; 10-K_2025-12-31_dva-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 213; calculation B01; calculation B02

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Free cash flow is durable enough to service debt but not to fund buybacks and partner distributions together: in nine months 2026 repurchases and partner distributions were 1.24x free cash flow before distributions. Development capital expenditure of USD 164 million and the buyback are the discretionary levers, and operating lease liabilities of USD 2,623.311 million sit outside total debt.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2025-12-31_dva-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 135; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dva-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 3; calculation B08

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Rivalry is moderate and mostly for acquisitions, medical directors and clinical labor: the largest competitor, Fresenius Medical Care, also manufactures supplies, and DaVita competes with large and mid-size providers, private equity-backed kidney care providers and nephrologist-owned units. The credit effect is limited pressure on rates and some pressure on acquisition prices and wages.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Threat of new entrants is low to moderate in dialysis and higher in integrated kidney care, where non-traditional providers with capital are entering. Substitutes are transplantation, home dialysis and drug therapies; home dialysis is already about 18% of DaVita’s U.S. revenue and expanded hemodialysis is being rolled out, so substitution is a gradual volume risk, not an immediate one.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Buyer power is the dominant force: Medicare sets rates for 57% of revenue and commercial payors negotiate and redesign plans, which is why the profit-bearing 26% of revenue is the main credit exposure. Supplier power is moderate: minimum purchase commitments of USD 961.093 million in 2026 reduce flexibility, and some competitors manufacture their own supplies and may have cost advantages, but the company does not report a supplier dependence that would change liquidity.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Political and regulatory factors are the primary credit driver because regulation sets rates for most revenue: the transitional drug add-on for phosphate binders is set to expire at the end of 2026, CMS estimated a 2.7% reimbursement increase for 2027, the Department of Health and Human Services published a kidney care plan on 2026-10-20 on competition, transplantation and prevention, expired enhanced tax credits are cutting exchange enrollment and open government inquiries remain. Economic factors are wage inflation and commercial coverage; social factors are mortality and flu seasons that reduced 2025 volume; technological factors are middle-molecule therapies and GLP-1 and SGLT2 drugs. Each matters through revenue per treatment or treatment volume.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Strengths are scale and market share, regulated recurring revenue, low capital intensity, light maturities to 2029 and interest caps to 2028. Weaknesses are profit concentration in commercial payors, falling EBITDA margin, buybacks above free cash flow and negative total equity. Opportunities that could improve credit quality are slower buybacks, a 2.7% rate update for 2027, growth in risk-based integrated kidney care patients and early refinancing of the 2030 notes. Threats are commercial-mix erosion, wage inflation, the 2030 and 2031 wall, a step-down in the maximum leverage ratio after 2028 and open legal matters.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_dva-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 183; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dva-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 12; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dva-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 13; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dva-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 37

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The main credit supports are scale, regulated revenue, adequate cash conversion and near-term liquidity; the main constraints are leverage drifting up, margin compression, buybacks above free cash flow and the 2030 and 2031 maturities. The trend is mildly negative: debt to EBITDA of 3.36x at FY2024, 3.72x at FY2025 and 3.82x at 2026-09-30, with EBITDA margin down and buybacks slowing. Interest cover on cash interest fell to 5.35x in FY2025 from 6.65x, and accrual-based cover is 4.75x for the last twelve months. Key missing datapoints are profit by payor class, an agency rating, market pricing and the executed credit agreement.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Over the next 12 to 24 months the company expects approximately flat treatment volumes and has raised the low end of 2026 adjusted operating income guidance; tailwinds are rate updates of 2.2% and 2.7%, falling buybacks and interest caps through 2028, and headwinds are the expiry of enhanced premium tax credits, wage inflation, the end of the phosphate binder add-on in 2026 and any further payor mix loss. Leverage is likely to hold near 3.8x on the house measure if EBITDA stays flat and buybacks do not exceed free cash flow, which is a trend reading and not a forecast.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Over three to five years the 2030 and 2031 maturities, the step-down of caps to USD 500 million in 2030 and the step-down of the maximum leverage ratio to 4.50x after 2028 per the annual report bring refinancing and interest-cost risk together, while substitution by transplantation and drug therapies and the Department of Health and Human Services plan are slower structural uncertainties. International growth and integrated kidney care could add earnings but at lower margins.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The issuer-specific downside starts with further loss of commercial coverage through plan redesign, exchange attrition after the expiry of enhanced tax credits and employer responses to the Marietta decision, while wage and supply inflation continue. The first operational break is revenue per treatment falling or flattening while patient care cost per treatment keeps rising above 67.09% of revenue per treatment, which takes EBITDA margin below 19.90%.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_dva-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 61; 10-K_2025-12-31_dva-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 62; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dva-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 32; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dva-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 37

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The financial transmission is leverage: at unchanged debt, a 4.49% fall in last-twelve-months EBITDA takes the house measure to 4.00x and a 15.61% fall in Consolidated EBITDA takes the issuer ratio to 4.00x, where many limits on repurchases return, and free cash flow would fall below the USD 1,000 million low end of 2026 guidance. Liquidity would hold near term because cash and the undrawn revolver cover debt due before 2028 13.27x, and management levers are slowing or stopping buybacks, cutting development capital expenditure of USD 164 million and cutting partner buy-ins. Resilience looks sufficient to avoid liquidity distress through 2029, but the 2030 and 2031 maturities, 2.96x EBITDA, would then be refinanced at higher leverage and under a lower maximum ratio.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2025-12-31_dva-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 135; 10-K_2025-12-31_dva-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 183; EX-99.1_2026-10-29_dva93026ex991.htm.jsonl, page 3; EX-99.1_2026-10-29_dva93026ex991.htm.jsonl, page 15; calculation B04; calculation B05; calculation B06; calculation B07

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Overall, DaVita presents an adequate business profile supported by scale, regulated recurring revenue and low capital intensity, but credit quality is constrained by profit concentration in commercial payors, rising leverage and buybacks above free cash flow. Cash-flow durability appears adequate because free cash flow before partner distributions is 47.50% of EBITDA, though thinner after distributions. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on commercial mix, EBITDA margin and leverage when the 2030 and 2031 maturities arrive. The primary downside path is commercial-mix and cost erosion lifting leverage toward 4.00x. Further analysis would require profit by payor class, the executed credit agreement, an agency rating and market pricing. Fundamental credit completed. Top risk: loss of commercial-payor profit lifting leverage ahead of the 2030 and 2031 maturities.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation B01; calculation B04
